case.summary: Case HHG-011 has been evaluated as fraud with a calibrated probability of 0.85, following a distinct card-testing sequence of 14 small online transactions followed by 34 larger ones. The activity originated online from a new device (SM-G610F running Chrome 66 for Android) that shares a device family with 352 other cards in the window, while the customer explicitly denies making the transaction. Historical indicators strongly support this verdict, showing prior confirmed-fraud cases associated with both this card tuple and the customer on a different card. This pattern closely mirrors prior confirmed-fraud cases such as CC-1593 and CC-0606, which also involved unauthorized online purchases originating from new devices. In response to these findings, the policy engine has triggered a series of required actions, including blocking the card, creating a case, filing a report, monitoring connected cards, and initiating step-up authentication.

sar.narrative: Suspicious activity involving card testing and subsequent unauthorized charges was identified under Case ID HHG-011, resulting in a total financial exposure of $3,984.80. The transaction sequence exhibited a classic card-testing shape consisting of 14 sub-$5 online transactions followed by 34 larger follow-up transactions within the observation window. The activity originated from an online channel using a newly flagged device (Samsung SM-G610F running Chrome 66.0 for Android) that shared a device family with 352 other cards during the same window. Risk indicators included a prior confirmed fraud history associated with both the card tuple and the customer on a different card, alongside an online transaction amount deviating significantly from typical spending patterns. The customer explicitly denied making the transaction, leading to the classification of the verdict as fraud. This pattern bears strong operational similarity to prior confirmed fraud cases retrieved from the graph, such as Case CC-1593 and Case CC-0606, which also featured unauthorized card-not-present purchases executed via newly introduced devices. Appropriate risk mitigation and case documentation procedures have been initiated in accordance with institutional policy.
